links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on pelvic congestion syndrome versus sixth-grade recommended level
links.effect: All chatbot responses significantly exceeded the sixth-grade level recommended by AMA and NIH (p < .001); Perplexity produced the most complex responses, Gemini was most readable on most indices.
links.quote: Readability analyses revealed that all chatbot responses significantly exceeded the sixth-grade level recommended by the AMA and NIH (p < .001).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the readability, quality, and reliability of patient-facing medical information generated by three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, Perplexity) on pelvic congestion syndrome without testing a deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
